CLAUDE.md

Source: CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

Shared conventions

The portfolio’s shared rules are synced into .claude/shared/ from pedrobtz/packages:claude/shared/. Never edit them here. Where this file and a shared file disagree, this file wins for this package.

@.claude/shared/workflow.md @.claude/shared/r-package.md @.claude/shared/ci.md @.claude/shared/native-code.md @.claude/shared/correctness.md @.claude/shared/assurance.md

What this is

zufast is a header-only library of small, portable C99 primitives for the hot path between external text or bytes and native values: number parsing and formatting, ISO 8601 dates, booleans, UUIDs, hex, Base64, XXH3, float16 and endian helpers, UTF-8 validation and 128-bit integers. Other packages consume it through LinkingTo: zufast alone and carry their own copy of the code, so zufast is never a run-time dependency. The fast_*() R functions exist to test, benchmark and demonstrate the C layer. Zero hard runtime dependencies. Time zones, UUID generation, cryptography, containers and Unicode normalisation are permanent non-goals (design §2); anything new must pass the admission test there, with a named consumer.

.agents/design.md is the specification and outranks this file. Benchmark results live in .agents/benchmarks.md.

Current state

Verified 2026-11-11. 0.1.0 is on CRAN (published 2026-10-21). The default branch is 0.1.0.9000 and carries the 0.1.1 work in NEWS.md: ISO week dates, expanded-year parsing (ZUF_DT_EXPANDED_YEAR) and zufast/wide.h. All three stage issues are closed; 0.1.1 is not yet submitted. Still deferred, until a consumer asks: varints, CRC32C, HTTP dates, _opt forms of the 128-bit parsers, week-date parsing and SIMD paths (design §25).

Versions and dependents

The current version’s parent issue is #34 for v0.1.1, with zutempo as its named consumer. Sibling packages that build against the headers, listed in tools/revdep/consumers.txt: zubin, zudedup, zumsgpack, zunpy, zupdf, zusvg and zutoml. Adoption issues in zuxlsx, zuyaml, zucbor, zuhttp and zucsv are tracked in design §3.2.

Commands

All are run from the package root and are occasional; the everyday loop is the shared devtools set.

tools/check-headers           # header gate: standalone C99/C++11, -Werror (§21.1)
tools/run-symbol-audit        # compiled-code NOTE audit of the full-use probe (§21.3)
tools/run-fuzz [target ...]   # libFuzzer + ASan/UBSan, canary first (§21.5)
tools/run-parse-corpus        # Nigel Tao's number corpus; network (§21.4)
tools/run-revdep [name ...]   # build every consumer against this tree
tools/run-benchmarks          # release build; record in .agents/benchmarks.md
tools/vendor/verify           # vendor tree against manifest and checksums

tools/vendor/fetch (network, maintainer only) and tools/vendor/record regenerate the vendor tree and its checksums.

Architecture

  • inst/include/zufast.h and inst/include/zufast/*.h are the product, one header per area (layout in design §5). detail/ holds internal helpers and vendor_config.h, which configures the vendored code. vendor/ holds ffc.h, Ryu and xxHash.
  • src/ is a consumer of those headers like any other: zufast_r.c holds the .Call wrappers behind R/, and includes <zufast.h>. Because the package’s own shared object contains every primitive, CRAN’s sanitizer, valgrind, LTO and noLD flavours exercise the headers through it.
  • src/zufast_test.c is an always-compiled test harness (zufast_test_* symbols) that drives each C function with caller-chosen buffer capacities. zufast_test_wide.c and zufast_test_wide_fallback.c compile one wide.h harness twice, natively and with ZUF_NO_INT128.
  • src/init.c registers the entry points with R_useDynamicSymbols(FALSE) and R_forceSymbols(TRUE). There is no R_RegisterCCallable and no static archive, by design (§4).
  • tools/zufasttest is a fixture package in the exact shape of a consumer; tools/zufastbench is the benchmark package. tools/abi/ holds the header probes, tools/fuzz/ the fuzz targets and the pinned fast_float.
  • The C layer never raises. R-side argument checks raise classed conditions through zufast_abort() in R/conditions.R, all inheriting zufast_error.

Invariants that are easy to break

  • Every symbol a header emits is static inline. A global symbol would let two consumers loaded together bind to each other’s copy; plain static warns as unused under -Werror in a unit that does not call it (§4.5). test-abi.R asserts zufast.so exports only R_init_zufast.
  • Headers include only <stddef.h>, <stdint.h>, <stdbool.h> and <string.h>, and compile standalone as C99 and C++11 under -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror. Only the vendored Ryu units include more (§5).
  • No R header, SEXP or Rf_ anywhere under inst/include/, and no vendor identifier (ffc_, XXH, ryu) outside vendor/ and detail/vendor_config.h. No vendor type in a public declaration.
  • Nothing R CMD check forbids in compiled code (printf, abort, exit, rand, stdout, …) and no writable data: every table is const. A violation is a NOTE in every consumer, not in zufast, which is why tools/run-symbol-audit exists (§21.3, #23).
  • Source compatibility, not ABI (§4.4): a public function, type, macro or enumerator, once released, keeps its meaning, and enumerator values are permanent. The real gate is the reverse-dependency check of every consumer. zuf_int_ helpers are visible but outside this promise.
  • Every function is pure: no allocation, errno, locale, global state or time.h, so consumers may call it from any thread (§19.2).
  • zuf_result.ptr follows std::from_chars: one past the last byte on success and on ZUF_ERR_RANGE, equal to first on ZUF_ERR_INVALID. A parser never requires the whole span to be consumed (§7).
  • Prefixes: zuf_/ZUF_ public C, zuf_int_ internal, zufast_ entry points and condition classes, zufast_test_ test symbols, fast_ R. The family’s zu_ is zukomp’s and is never used here (§6).
  • Numbers are correctly rounded, not as.numeric()-exact (§8.4). There is no R-exact mode; the differences from base R are documented, not bugs.

Testing

  • External oracles: strtod and R_strtod() differentials, the Ryu vectors (fixtures/shortest-f64.tsv), xxHash’s published vectors (fixtures/xxh3-vectors.tsv, licence open in #25), Markus Kuhn’s UTF-8 stress cases, and R’s own date functions. The parse-number-fxx corpus is too large for the suite and runs weekly in parse-corpus.yaml. The full plan is design §21.4.
  • Helpers: one helper-<area>.R per test file, holding its .Call shims and constants so tests run shuffled. helper-codec.R holds R reference implementations of hex and Base64, so no Suggests dependency is needed. helper-wide.R calls both wide.h builds and requires identical results before returning any value. helper-abi.R reads the export table of the installed shared object with nm.
  • Budget: the design requires the suite to finish in under a minute.

Continuous integration

Shared r-actions workflows, pinned by commit: R-CMD-check.yaml (quick on a pull request, full after merge or with full-ci; adds Windows R-devel, NOSUGGESTS and NOLD, since a number parser must survive R without long double), native-checks.yml (sanitizers, valgrind, LTO, gctorture, rchk, analyzers, CRAN special flavours), coverage.yaml, hardening.yaml (the libFuzzer targets; weekly for 30 minutes), arch.yaml (i386, musl, big-endian s390x; weekly), vendor.yaml (tools/vendor/verify), vendor-upstream.yaml (opens an issue when an upstream releases) and revdep.yaml (every consumer, on header changes and weekly).

Package-owned workflows: abi.yaml runs tools/check-headers and the symbol audit, consumer.yaml installs tools/zufasttest, proves it holds no global zufast symbol and still loads with zufast uninstalled, parse-corpus.yaml runs the number corpus weekly, and zufastbench.yaml runs the benchmark package weekly. pkgdown.yaml builds the site.

Vendored native code

Pins and licences are in tools/vendor/manifest.tsv; patches are in tools/patches/<source>/, each named in the manifest, inst/COPYRIGHTS and cran-comments.md, and each submitted upstream (#24 for ffc 0004).

  • ffc.h (kolemannix/ffc.h, tag v26.09.01, MIT of its triple licence). Patches: 0001 adds the FFC_LINKAGE macros, 0002 drops the -Wfloat-equal pragmas, 0003 fixes the u64 overflow check at the maximum digit count, 0004 makes the lookup tables const.
  • Ryu (ulfjack/ryu, tag v2.0, BSL-1.0 of its dual licence). Patch 0001 turns d2s.c and f2s.c into static inline headers.
  • xxHash (Cyan4973/xxHash, tag v0.8.4, BSD-2-Clause; xxhash.h only). No patches.

The defines that configure each library (FFC_LINKAGE=static, XXH_INLINE_ALL, XXH_NO_STDLIB, RYU_ASSERT) live in inst/include/zufast/detail/vendor_config.h, and verify checks them against the manifest’s defines column. Upstream licence texts are installed under inst/licenses/.
